properties.decision:
ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-09-02: *"can we .gitignore the docs/feedback files? I don't want them appearing on the repo for the whole world to see. And storyflow is my own proprietary project that I don't want anybody to see."*

**THE ACT: `docs/feedback/` is added to .gitignore and its 11 tracked files are removed from the index with `git rm --cached` — they STAY ON DISK on his machine.** This is untracking, not deletion. He was asked and chose "keep locally, never commit".

DISTINCT FROM `dec:reflow2s-own-feedback-documents-are-removed-once-captured` (accepted 2026-08-15), and the difference is why this is a separate node:
· That decision DELETES the document, and its licence is CAPTURE — "once ingested, please remove". Its reason is tidiness: he did not want documents accumulating in a repo he has to clean up later.
· This one UNTRACKS the document and keeps it. Its reason is DISCLOSURE, and it does not depend on ingestion being complete, because nothing is lost — the file remains on his machine whether or not the graph has finished with it.
Both retire the Artifact from the BUILD's view; only the older one destroys the source. Applying the older policy to eleven documents whose ingestion nobody has verified would destroy sources under a licence never granted for them.

⚠️ **WHAT THIS DOES NOT ACHIEVE, measured 2026-09-02 and put to him before he chose.** The repository is PUBLIC and has been since 2026-07-17.
· The 11 files remain in git HISTORY and stay retrievable by anyone; `docs/feedback/2026-08-23-dev-storyflow-agent-feedback.md` has been public for ten days.
· **THE LARGER EXPOSURE IS NOT THESE FILES.** `docs/design/reflow2.json` is committed and public, and **275 of its 3,632 nodes name storyflow (643 mentions)** — the findings, facts and decisions that quote the fleet reports. Untracking the source documents does nothing about those.
He was shown all three wider options — make the repository private, rewrite history, or scrub the export — and chose the narrow one knowingly. THIS IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT LATER MISTAKEN FOR AN ASSURANCE THE CONTENT IS PRIVATE. It is not; it stops the bleeding forward only.

**MECHANICS, and why the Artifacts must move too.** These 11 documents are registered Artifacts. Untracking them makes `reflow2_check.py` fail with `missing_artifact` in CI, because the build no longer contains a file the design points at — measured today when `art:chama-genesis-feedback-2026-09-02` failed exactly that way. So each is RETIRED ON THE RECORD via OBSOLETES from this decision, which is what `expected_absence` reads: the two documents already retired under the 2026-08-15 policy show as notes rather than failures for precisely this reason.

The Artifacts keep their names and checksums — the proof of what was captured — and their Fragments and YIELDED edges, so every finding stays traceable to the document that produced it. What is retired is the claim that the BUILD contains the file. The file still exists; it is simply no longer somewhere this repository can see.

GOING FORWARD, his choice in the same exchange: new field reports are kept locally and never committed. A report can still be registered and its findings captured; the document itself does not enter the repository.
properties.name: Field reports are UNTRACKED and kept only on the author's machine — the repository is public and some of the projects reporting are proprietary
properties.rationale:
Recorded separately rather than as a second application of the 2026-08-15 policy because the licence is different and a later reader must be able to tell which one governs. That policy's condition is "once ingested" — it trades the document for its capture. This decision needs no such condition: the file survives on his machine, so untracking costs nothing recoverable.

Kept honest about its limits on purpose. A decision that said only "field reports are private now" would read, in six months, as a statement that the content is not public. It is public, it stays public, and the two measurements above are in the decision text so nobody has to re-derive them to know that.
